# Built-in Macros

The macros that come with the language, usable in every file without an import. They are written in Vidar, in `src/prelude.vidar`; a declaration of your own with the same name takes precedence. Chapter 10, [Built-in Macros](ch10-00-builtin-macros.md), introduces them.

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`scoped!`](#scoped) | scoped! |
| [`with_allocator!`](#with_allocator) | with_allocator!(a) { ... |
| [`locked!`](#locked) | locked!(&mutex) { ... |
| [`timed!`](#timed) | timed!("label") { ... |
| [`track!`](#track) | track!("label") { ... |
| [`do!`](#do) | do! |
| [`comptime!`](#comptime) | comptime! |
| [`dbg!`](#dbg) | dbg!(expr) prints "file:line: expr = value" (to stderr) and evaluates to the value. |
| [`check!`](#check) | check!(cond) panics when cond is false, showing the expression; for comparisons it also shows both operands. |
| [`move!`](#move) | move!(x) evaluates to x's value and leaves x zero: it moves a value with impl Destroy to a new owner (a variable, a field, an #owned parameter) instead of copying it. |
| [`todo!`](#todo) | todo!() / todo!("message"): panic in code that isn't written yet. |
| [`unimplemented!`](#unimplemented) | unimplemented!() / unimplemented!("message"): panic in code that is deliberately not supported. |

## `scoped!`

```odin
scoped :: proc!(allocator: Expr = context.allocator, body: Stmt) -> Stmt
```

scoped! { ... } gives the block its own temp allocator and frees it when the block ends.
scoped!(allocator) { ... } takes the arena's memory from `allocator` instead of context.allocator.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	for round in 0..<3 {
		scoped! {
			label := fmt.tprintf("round %d", round)   // from the block's own temp allocator
			fmt.println(label)
		}                                           // freed here
	}
}
```

```output
round 0
round 1
round 2
```

See [Memory and Scope](ch10-01-memory-and-scope.md#scoped-a-temp-allocator-for-a-block).

## `with_allocator!`

```odin
with_allocator :: proc!(allocator: Expr, body: Stmt) -> Stmt
```

with_allocator!(a) { ... } makes `a` the block's context.allocator.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	arena: mem.Arena
	buf: [512]byte
	mem.arena_init(&arena, buf[:])
	with_allocator!(mem.arena_allocator(&arena)) {
		xs := make([dynamic]int)          // from the arena
		append(&xs, 1, 2, 3)
		fmt.println(xs[:], arena.offset > 0)
	}
}
```

```output
[1, 2, 3] true
```

## `locked!`

```odin
locked :: proc!(mutex: Expr, body: Stmt) -> Stmt
```

locked!(&mutex) { ... } holds the lock for the block and releases it on every exit.

```vidar
Account :: struct {
	mu:      sync.Mutex,
	balance: int,
}

withdraw :: proc(a: ^Account, amount: int) -> bool {
	locked!(&a.mu) {
		if a.balance < amount do return false   // unlocked here too
		a.balance -= amount
	}
	return true
}

main :: proc() {
	a := Account{balance = 100}
	fmt.println(withdraw(&a, 30), withdraw(&a, 500), a.balance)
}
```

```output
true false 70
```

## `timed!`

```odin
timed :: proc!(label: Expr = "", body: Stmt) -> Stmt
```

timed!("label") { ... } prints how long the block took (to stderr). The label defaults to the call site.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	timed!("build table") {
		table: [1000]int
		for i in 0..<len(table) do table[i] = i * i
		fmt.println(table[999])
	}
}
```

```output
998001
```

It also prints `[timed] build table: ...` with the time to stderr.

## `track!`

```odin
track :: proc!(a: Expr = "", b: Expr = "", body: Stmt) -> Stmt
```

track!("label") { ... } runs the block with a tracking context.allocator and, when it ends, prints
every allocation that is still live (to stderr). The label defaults to the call site.
Only in -debug builds; otherwise the block runs untracked.
track!(allocator) / track!(allocator, "label") tracks allocations made from `allocator` instead.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	track!("parse") {
		kept := make([]int, 8)       // still live when the block ends
		tmp := make([]int, 4)
		delete(tmp)
		_ = kept
	}
}
```

Built with `-debug`, the block's end prints the allocation that was never freed, `kept`'s 64 bytes, with its location, to stderr. Without `-debug` the block runs untracked.

## `do!`

```odin
do :: proc!(T: Type = _, body: Stmt) -> Expr
```

do! { ...; take value } evaluates to the value the block takes. The block runs just before the enclosing
statement. do!(T) { ... } gives the result type when it can't be inferred from the taken values.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	scores := []int{72, 95, 88}
	best := do! {
		top := 0
		for s in scores do top = max(top, s)
		take top
	}
	grade := do! {
		if best >= 90 do take "A"
		take "B"
	}
	fmt.println(best, grade)
}
```

```output
95 A
```

See [Blocks That Produce a Value](ch10-03-do-blocks.md).

## `comptime!`

```odin
comptime :: proc!(body: Stmt) -> Expr
```

comptime! { expr } / comptime! { ...; take value } runs the block in the transpiler and folds to its value:
calls in it run at compile time, as if each had a '!'.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	mask := comptime! { (1 << 12) - 1 }
	squares: [5]int = comptime! {
		out: [dynamic]int
		for i in 0..<5 do append(&out, i * i)
		take out
	}
	fmt.println(mask, squares)
}
```

```output
4095 [0, 1, 4, 9, 16]
```

See [Running Code at Compile Time](ch11-03-compile-time-evaluation.md#comptime-blocks).

## `dbg!`

```odin
dbg :: proc!(value: Expr) -> Expr
```

dbg!(expr) prints "file:line: expr = value" (to stderr) and evaluates to the value.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	width, height := 3, 4
	area := dbg!(width * height) * 2
	fmt.println(area)
}
```

```output
24
```

On stderr: `[main.vidar:3] width * height = 12`.

## `check!`

```odin
check :: proc!(cond: Expr, message: Expr = "") -> Stmt
```

check!(cond) panics when cond is false, showing the expression; for comparisons it also
shows both operands. check!(cond, "message") adds a message.

```vidar,should_panic
main :: proc() {
	xs := []int{1, 2, 3}
	check!(len(xs) > 0)
	check!(xs[0] + xs[1] == xs[2], "sums")
	check!(len(xs) == 4)
}
```

```error
panic: check failed: len(xs) == 4
	len(xs) = 3
```

## `move!`

```odin
move :: proc!(x: Expr) -> Expr
```

move!(x) evaluates to x's value and leaves x zero: it moves a value with impl Destroy to a new owner
(a variable, a field, an #owned parameter) instead of copying it.

```vidar
Box :: struct { name: string }

box_destroy :: proc(b: ^Box) {
	if b.name != "" do fmt.println("destroy", b.name)
}

impl Destroy for Box { destroy = box_destroy }

main :: proc() {
	a := Box{"crate"}
	b := move!(a)                // b owns it; a is zero
	fmt.println(a.name == "", b.name)
}
```

```output
true crate
destroy crate
```

See [Owners, Borrows and Moves](ch07-02-ownership.md#moving-with-move).

## `todo!`

```odin
todo :: proc!(message: Expr = "") -> Expr
```

todo!() / todo!("message"): panic in code that isn't written yet.

```vidar,should_panic
parse_header :: proc(data: []byte) -> int {
	todo!("headers")
}

main :: proc() {
	fmt.println(parse_header({}))
}
```

```error
panic: not yet implemented: headers
```

## `unimplemented!`

```odin
unimplemented :: proc!(message: Expr = "") -> Expr
```

unimplemented!() / unimplemented!("message"): panic in code that is deliberately not supported.

```vidar,should_panic
encode :: proc(format: string) -> string {
	switch format {
	case "json": return "{}"
	}
	unimplemented!("only json")
}

main :: proc() {
	fmt.println(encode("json"))
	fmt.println(encode("xml"))
}
```

```output
{}
```

```error
panic: not implemented: only json
```
